answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to lock a time-bound stake that only unlocks after sustained honest work, like a willow bending with the tide instead of snapping. A flood of fake accounts must tie up real capital for weeks, and misbehavior burns part of the stake, so each fake identity costs money and time while honest agents keep a small ember of reputation that grows with every verified task, pricing cheap fakes out of the market.
